summary: Close to the run boundary, with all obligations disposed and no pending work, this is a minimal learning-saving step: a factual check of the legacy peers-file helper module plus an explicit statement of what the run retained. Submission is action=research adding one source (S-peersjson, peersjson.go 18-67) and feedback; no map version is created. Factual addition: peersjson.go exports only ReadPeersJSON and ReadConfigJSON, both parsing a legacy JSON peers or configuration file, and neither has a caller anywhere in the non-test sources, so they are caller-facing migration helpers rather than part of any protocol path; the module was not otherwise read, so its parsing and validation behaviour stays unmapped and it is explicitly not claimed to be safe or unsafe. Retained-state statement: map v4 with the added F-log-watermark Fact, the b-append-entries produce/consume edges to it, the corrected transport classification and the corrected target_profile injection statement; three confirmed in-scope violations - the truncation-failure watermark, the installSnapshot stale watermark and the snapshot-trigger underflow - each with an executed check and a reviewed correspondence; one reviewed bounded no-violation for the configuration rollback; no pending work and no open review issues. The remaining list names what is actually open so a later step does not have to guess: peersjson.go's readers are unevaluated and unmapped, the composed store-failure-plus-compaction history was argued by reading but never executed as one witness, the installSnapshot non-monotonic compaction variant was reasoned but not exercised, the malformed-entry panic lead (DecodeConfiguration and prepareLog's default, with no recover anywhere) has no execution witness and sits outside the crash-stop fault model, and the transport reading described behaviour without evaluating it for defects. Preflight validation returns valid with no diagnostics.
